NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

  Peninsula Seniors

  City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by

  agenda. If you would like to address the City Council, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the
  City Clerk. Under the State's open meeting law - the Brown Act - no action may be taken on any item not

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 25, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR HUFF at 7:01 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Margie Beierschmitt, Executive Director of Peninsula Seniors.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

None.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 4A-E AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF APRIL 2023

  APPROVED WARRANTS 66145 THROUGH 66195 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $342,557.07, AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040123 THROUGH
  040323 IN THE AMOUNT OF $120,365.77 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $462,922.84 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF APRIL 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF APRIL 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
APRIL 25, 2023
 E.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 11, 2023

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Public comment received by Ellen Orenstein regarding traffic concerns on Deep Valley Drive,
and Barbara Katsu regarding traffic concerns on Deep Valley Drive, and concerns about a lack
of maintenance on the grounds of the Town and Country Shopping Center.

**ITEM TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: 19TH AMENDMENT
  COMMEMORATION PLAQUE PROPOSAL

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the proposed plaque and location for
  installation of the 19th Amendment commemoration in the amount of $3,000 and direct
  staff on funding the project through either solicited donations to the Foundation or
  through a combination of solicited donations and existing Pepper Tree Foundation
  funds.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from Palos Verdes Peninsula League of Women Voters
Copresident Janet Herman.

  APPROVE THE PROPOSED PLAQUE AND LOCATION FOR INSTALLATION
  OF THE 19TH AMENDMENT COMMEMORATION IN THE AMOUNT OF $3,000
  AND DIRECT STAFF TO FUND THE PROJECT THROUGH A COMBINATION
  OF SOLICITED DONATIONS AND EXISTING PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION
  FUNDS.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Huff so ordered.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230148
  AMENDMENTS TO THE 2021-2029 HOUSING ELEMENT OF THE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES 2040 GENERAL PLAN
  LOCATION: CITYWIDE

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1.) Open the Public Hearing; 2.) Take public
  testimony; 3.) Discuss the issues; 4.) Find that the proposed Resolution No. 2543 is
  exempt from the provisions of CEQA; and 5.) Adopt Resolution No. 2543, making
  findings related to and adopting General Plan Amendment No. 230149 to the 2021-
  2029 Housing Element of the Rolling Hills Estates 2040 General Plan.

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, to open the public hearing.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 25, 2023
   COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, to close the public hearing.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2543, MAKING FINDINGS RELATED TO AND
  ADOPTING GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT NO. 230149 TO THE 2021-2029
  HOUSING ELEMENT OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES 2040 GENERAL
  PLAN, AND FINDING THE PROPOSED RESOLUTION NO. 2543 EXEMPT
  FROM THE PROVISIONS OF CEQA.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  CITY COMMITTEE COMPOSITION

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the composition of the City’s
  Committees and provide direction if any changes are desired.

City Clerk Pettit provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

City Manager Grammer confirmed that currently there is one Park and Activities Commissioner
that also serves on the Pepper Tree Foundation Fundraising Committee, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

Discussion ensued about Committee Member absences and ability to achieve a quorum at
meetings.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

Consensus to receive and file.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

B.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION WEBPAGE

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file this report.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked staff for their work on the updates to this webpage.
He recommended that staff return with ideas for recognizing Native Americans as well
Japanese Americans, possibly at the Nature Center.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA concurred with COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’s
suggestions for additional recognitions.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

Consensus to receive and file.

C.  KNOW YOUR ZONE WEBSITE (PVPready)

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file this report.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 25, 2023
 COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested coordinating evacuation drills of neighborhoods
throughout the City each year.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA emphasized the importance of knowing your zone ahead of
time, since there may not be power, access to the internet or even cell service in an emergency.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

Consensus to receive and file.

D.  REQUEST TO ENTER INTO AN AMENDED “MEASURE M FUNDING AGREEMENT
  MULTI-YEAR SUB REGIONAL PROGRAM” WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY (LACMTA)

  Recommendation: That the City Council enter into an amended Measure M Funding
  Agreement (Amendment No. 1) Multi-Year Sub Regional Program, with the Los Angeles
  County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA), in the grand total amount of
  $2,880,252.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public Works Director Wahba explained that traffic impact fees are ongoing and that there are
other funding sources available that will be considered before going out to bid, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

Public Works Director Wahba confirmed the horse trail will not be moved, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE AMENDED MEASURE M FUNDING AGREEMENT (AMENDMENT
  NO. 1) MULTI-YEAR SUB REGIONAL PROGRAM, WITH THE LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY (LACMTA), IN
  THE GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $2,880,252.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ attended the California Contract Cities Association’s (CCCA)
dinner for outgoing President Jeff Wood.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN noted the Southern California Association of Governments
(SCAG) General Assembly will be held May 4-5, CCCA’s Annual Municipal Seminar May 18-
21.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER will be attending the West Basin Water District 2023 Water
Issues Forum on May 5.

MAYOR HUFF attended the Cal Cities Leadership Summit in Sacramento as well as the State
Board of Directors meeting.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 25, 2023
 12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION VACANCY APPOINTMENT

MAYOR HUFF announced that Margaret Johnson has been appointed to the Park and
Activities Commission. MAYOR HUFF indicated that interviews were conducted to fill the
vacant seat at a special City Council meeting held earlier this evening.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:24 PM MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting to Tuesday, May 9, 2023, at
7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Britt Huff
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
APRIL 25, 2023
